Perturbing already-trained prefixes—shuffling order, truncating history, masking recent items—measures the fitted model’s sensitivity on those inputs. Interpretation: performance drops suggest reliance on the changed information; they do not establish useful temporal reasoning, memorization, or future generalization. Prefix targets already used in optimization remain in-sample, and perturbations can create unrealistic histories. Chronological evaluation research also shows that per-user ordering does not guarantee global temporal separation and that splitting choices can change model rankings. Keep the benchmark’s pinned splits and describe these limits. [Gusak et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16289)

Use diagnostic findings to propose a small, explicit training ablation; confirm usefulness through the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10, with identical users, candidates, and evaluation seed. Repeatedly choosing experiments from validation results makes validation adaptive: the winning score can become optimistic. Logging all trials and limiting comparisons improves transparency but does not remove selection bias; ordinary validation reuse lacks the guarantees of specialized reusable-holdout mechanisms. Final generalization evidence must come from the host’s untouched held-out evaluation. [Dwork et al., 2015](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2015/hash/bad5f33780c42f2588878a9d07405083-Abstract.html)

For descriptive uncertainty, adapt paired bootstrap resampling: retain each user’s baseline/candidate hit indicators, resample the same user indices for both models within each category, then average the four category-level HR@10 differences equally. Report the observed difference and bootstrap interval alongside the pinned selection score. This estimates user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates; it does not capture training variability, candidate-sampling variability, or correct adaptive-selection bias. [Paired-bootstrap foundation: Koehn, 2004](https://aclanthology.org/W04-3250/)
